column1: It is not easy to be systematic and objective about language study.
column2: 在语言研究中做到系统而客观并不容易。

column1: Popular linguistic debate regularly deteriorates into invective and polemic.
column2: 常见的语言争论往往演变为激烈攻击和争辩。

column1: Language belongs to everyone, so most people feel they have a right to hold an opinion about it.
column2: 语言属于所有人，因此大多数人认为自己有权对语言问题发表看法。

column1: And when opinions differ, emotions can run high.
column2: 当意见不一致时，情绪可能变得激烈。

column1: Arguments can start as easily over minor points of usage as over major policies of linguistic education.
column2: 关于语言的争论可能从用法上的细微问题，轻易地发展到语言教育的重大政策问题。

column1: Language, moreover, is a very public behaviour, so it is easy for different usages to be noted and criticised.
column2: 此外，语言作为一种非常公开的行为，不同用法很容易被注意到并受到批评。

column1: No part of society or social behaviour is exempt: linguistic factors influence how we judge personality, intelligence, social status, educational standards, job aptitude, and many other areas of identity and social survival.
column2: 社会的任何领域、任何一种社会行为都受语言的影响。语言因素影响着我们如何判断一个人的性格、智力、社会地位、受教育水平和工作才能，也影响我们对身份认同和社会生存的许多其他方面的判断。
column13: social survival|n. 在社会中生存

column1: As a result, it is easy to hurt, and to be hurt, when language use is unfeelingly attacked.
column2: 因此，当语言使用受到无情的攻击时，就很容易受到伤害。而当语言遭到这样的攻击时，人们也会感到痛苦。

column1: In its most general sense, prescriptivism is the view that one variety of language has an inherently higher value than others, and that this ought to be imposed on the whole of the speech community.
column2: 从最广泛的意义上讲，规范主义认为某种语言形式本身就具有更高的价值，而这种价值应该被推广到整个语言使用群体之中。

column1: The view is propounded especially in relation to grammar and vocabulary, and frequently with reference to pronunciation.
column2: 这种观点尤其体现在语法和词汇方面，常涉及发音。

column1: The variety which is favoured, in this account, is usually a version of the standard written language, especially as encountered in literature, or in the formal spoken language which most closely reflects this style.
column2: 按照这种看法，受到推崇的语言变体通常是标准书面语的一种形式，尤其指文学作品中的书面语，或是最接近这种文体的正式口语。
column5: in this account|按照这种看法
column7: standard written language|n. 标准书面语
column9: formal spoken language|n. 正式口语

column1: Adherents to this variety are said to speak or write ‘correctly’; deviations from it are said to be ‘incorrect’.
column2: 遵循这种语言变体的人，被认为说得或写得“正确”；偏离这种变体的用法，则被认为是“错误的”。

column1: All the main languages have been studied prescriptively, especially in the 18th century approach to the writing of grammars and dictionaries.
column2: 各种主要语言都曾有人从规范主义的角度加以研究，这在18世纪编写语法书和词典的方式中表现得尤为明显。
column4: prescriptively|adv. 从规范主义的角度

column1: The aims of these early grammarians were threefold: (a) they wanted to codify the principles of their languages, to show that there was a system beneath the apparent chaos of usage, (b) they wanted a means of settling disputes over usage, and (c) they wanted to point out what they felt to be common errors, in order to ‘improve’ the language.
column2: 这些早期语法学家有三个目的：第一，把各自语言的原则整理成系统，表明看似混乱的用法其实有规律可循；第二，找到一种解决用法争议的办法；第三，指出他们所认为的常见错误，以便“改进”语言。
column9: apparent chaos|n. 表面上的混乱

column1: The authoritarian nature of the approach is best characterised by its reliance on ‘rules’ of grammar.
column2: 这种方法的专制性质主要体现在其对‘语法规则’的依赖上。

column1: Some usages are ‘prescribed’, to be learnt and followed accurately; others are ‘proscribed’, to be avoided.
column2: 有些用法是‘必须遵循的’，需要准确学习和遵循；另一些用法则是‘应避免的’。

column1: In this early period, there were no half-measures: usage was either right or wrong, and it was the task of the grammarian not simply to record alternatives, but to pronounce judgement upon them.
column2: 在那个早期阶段，并没有什么‘半途而废’的中间状态：用法要么正确，要么错误，语法学家的任务不仅是记录替代方案，更是对它们作出判断。

column1: These attitudes are still with us, and they motivate a widespread concern that linguistic standards should be maintained.
column2: 这些态度至今仍然存在，它们引发了一种普遍的担忧：语言标准应该得到维护。

column1: Nevertheless, there is an alternative point of view that is concerned less with standards than with the facts of linguistic usage.
column2: 尽管如此，仍有一种不同的观点，更关注语言实际使用中的事实，而非语言标准。

column1: This approach is summarised in the statement that it is the task of the grammarian to describe, not prescribe -to record the facts of linguistic diversity, and not to attempt the impossible tasks of evaluating language variation or halting language change.
column2: 这种做法可以用一句话概括：语法学家的职责是描述语言，而非规定语言应当怎样使用。也就是说，要记录语言多样性的事实，无需尝试去做那些不可能做到的事：评判语言变异，或阻止语言演变。

column1: In the second half of the 18th century, we already find advocates of this view, such as Joseph Priestley, whose Rudiments of English Grammar (1761) insists that ‘the custom of speaking is the original and only just standard of any language’.
column2: 在18世纪后半期，已经有一些人支持这种观点了，比如约瑟夫·普里斯特利。他在《英语语法基础》（1761年出版）一书中指出：‘说话的习惯才是任何语言的原始且唯一的标准。’

column1: Linguistic issues, it is argued, cannot be solved by logic and legislation.
column2: 有人认为，语言问题无法通过逻辑或立法来解决。

column1: And this view has become the tenet of the modern linguistic approach to grammatical analysis.
column2: 这种观点已成为现代语言学语法分析方法的核心理念。

column1: In our own time, the opposition between ‘descriptivists’ and ‘prescriptivists’ has often become extreme, with both sides painting unreal pictures of the other.
column2: 在我们这个时代，‘描述主义者’与‘规范主义者’之间的对立往往变得极端，双方都描绘出对方虚假的形象。

column1: Descriptive grammarians have been presented as people who do not care about standards, because of the way they see all forms of usage as equally valid.
column2: 描写派语法学家把各种语言用法都视为同样合理。正因为如此，他们被描绘成不在乎语言规范的人。

column1: Prescriptive grammarians have been presented as blind adherents to a historical tradition.
column2: 规定派语法学家则被描绘成盲目追随某一历史传统的人。

column1: The opposition has even been presented in quasi-political terms - of radical liberalism vs elitist conservatism.
column2: 人们甚至用近乎政治化的措辞来描述这种对立，将其说成激进自由主义与精英保守主义的对抗。
